sources.currency_use: Provider cross-rate formula: reporting amount divided by primary-to-reporting exchange rate, then multiplied by primary-to-target rate. Match known currencies and coherent quote dates, verify stock/flow horizon and security-price currency separately, and retain per-leg actual/carried provenance without an unsupported equal-type or AR-only filter. Exact catalog-listed G_EXRT_DLY and G_EXRT_MTH are available candidates, not prevalidated coverage.

sources.title: Stata mean: estimates and standard errors of means
sources.use: Native e-class mean estimation can summarize one observation per fitted group, with uncertainty across the group coefficient distribution; keep actual group weighting and sample definition.

sources.title: S&P Research Insight North America Data Guide (2004): Currency Translation Rate
sources.use: Defines a balance-sheet-date currency translation rate, but this page does not establish multiplication versus division or reliability of the local CURRTR values. Do not infer a USD arithmetic rule from the label alone. See cached Xpressfeed currency chapter for explicit cross-rate formula.

sources.title: CRSP US Stock and US Index Data Descriptions Guide (March 29, 2012)
sources.use: Provider-authored guide hosted by UNIST library; defines legacy two-digit share types and exchange codes. Contemporary primary-site/WRDS URLs returned404; this complete131-page mirror downloaded and parsed successfully.

sources.title: CRSP/Compustat Merged Database Guide (May 14, 2013)
sources.use: Provider-authored guide: LINKTYPE and LINKPRIM code meanings, company-versus-security links, effective dates. Indexed WRDS copy returned404; complete university-mirror PDF downloaded and parsed. Also documents X-suffix LIID placeholders for earlier company-level ranges; see dummy_iid_physical_pages.
sources.dummy_iid_use: Physical p. 19 / printed p. 15 explains the dummy IID ending in X when Compustat company history predates issue-level security data; physical p. 21 / printed p. 17 defines LIID as an X-suffix placeholder for a period with company data but no identified Compustat security. Use only within the recorded dates and retain the linked PERMNO/date checks.

sources.title: S&P Research Insight North America Data Guide (2004): PRCCF/A199
sources.use: Fiscal-year closing price definition, split/stock-dividend presentation and last-trading close when suspended. Historical Canadian($T) price currency is CAD; this does not itself identify every modern price currency.

sources.title: S&P Xpressfeed and Research Insight: EPS and split adjustments
sources.use: EPSPX/AJEX formula: physical29/printed21. Unadjusted price/share delivery: physical107–108/printed99–100. Do not assume cumulative adjustment factors share a terminal base across providers. Research Insight2004 physical647/printed597 defines AJEX A27; physical659–660/printed609–610 maps EPSPX toA58 and discusses the1997 primary/basic convention change. Research Insight defaults differ from raw Xpressfeed.

sources.title: Thomson Reuters I/B/E/S Detail History User Guide (December2009)
sources.use: Detail estimates received in nondefault currencies are converted to company-level currency. Received-currency flags and stored value currency differ. Split-unadjusted product status does not imply no currency conversion. Verify each Summary/Actual product separately; do not infer currency from US file membership.

sources.title: WRDS: A Note on IBES Unadjusted Data (November2006)
sources.use: Provider methods: split-effective dates can differ from true event dates; adjusted/unadjusted Detail ratios can suffer rounding or unmatched records. Method3 physical6 and continuation7 puts an unadjusted actual on the estimate-date basis by multiplying by CFACSHR_est/CFACSHR_report. General anchor conversion uses anchor factor/value-date factor. This does not establish a shared absolute terminal base between CRSP and IBES, or authorize replacing a paper baseline product.

sources.title: Xpressfeed daily FX provenance and price timing clarification
sources.use: Daily EXRATTPD distinguishes actual vs carried-forward quote provenance, not different currency units. A missing descriptor does not erase an observed positive EXRATD with known FROM/TO/date. Daily and monthly price conversion are both listed: fiscal-close daily rate is a point-date choice; EXRAT1M is prescribed for monthly price data. Root earlier characterized EXRAT1M as flow-only; that assertion was incorrect and corrected before A3 real-activity finalization.

sources.title: CRSP historical versus header SIC codes
sources.use: Historical end-of-period SIC is date-specific; missing SIC represented aszero beforeMarch2000, validcodes100..9999. HeaderHSICCD is lastnonzero SIC and must not silently backfill historical periods. A SIC change creates a new name structure effective until next change/securityobsolescence; verify exact table dates andunique matching.

sources.title: Audit Analytics: SOX302 disclosure controls product and issue taxonomy
sources.use: Provider describes SOX302 assessments beginning2002, overlapping general-control/accounting issue categories, and effective controls with IT issues below material-weakness severity. This doesnot establish exact numeric MATERIAL_WEAKNESS codes. Local catalog has separate FEED10_SOX_302_DISCLOSURE_CONTRO and FEED11_SOX_404_INTERNAL_CONTROLS; W3126000559 requires302 and inherited404 route needs correction. WRDS public product page dictionary link redirects to login.

sources.title: WRDS CCM link boundary examples
sources.use: WRDS provider examples explicitly allow LINKDT=.B and LINKENDDT=.E (SIZE_BM), or missing start/end bounds (CCM). SAS special missings arebelowdates, so direct end>=date rejectsopenend. Root exactlocal ccmxpf_linktable audit foundNOmissing/specialLINKDT but14750 .E enddates;1179 P/C LC/LUopenendrows overlap1963–1994. Evidence isnot a countofaffectedanalysisrows.

sources.title: Compustat header IID versus dated primary issue
sources.use: Local FUNDA IID is labeled Header Primary Global Issue ID. The 2004 guide describes legacy monthly company market data as primary-issue data; modern SEC_MTHPRC has issue-level keys. Verify dated SEC_MTH.PRIMISS and issue/date-specific prices/currencies instead of treating header IID as a historical security assignment. CF-prediction A3 bounded audit found 647 header/datetime primary differences among 10500 final rows; dated primary monthly prices matched annual PRCC_F within0.005 on10495/10496 comparable rows, with daily/monthly currencies agreeing throughout. The same catalog labels HIID as Historic Primary Global Issue ID; verify its date-specific coverage before use. Mconserv A1 demonstrated header matching can exclude an entire historical period even where dated CCM primary links exist.

sources.title: CRSP historical and header CUSIP definitions
sources.location: Historical end-of-period CUSIP and latest/header NCUSIP
sources.use: The historical end-of-period CUSIP is available beginning 1968-01-02; CUSIPs are unavailable in CRSP name history before 1968. The latest/header NCUSIP is a distinct field. A dated CRSP name-history CUSIP cannot support a 1951–1961 link.

sources.title: S&P Research Insight CUSIP issuer and issue definitions (2004)
sources.location: CUSIP Number / issuer and issue code composition
sources.use: Compustat CUSIP identifies issuer and issue, but Compustat-assigned identifiers use synthetic issuer codes (99 in positions 4–5) and issue numbers beginning 93. This is not evidence of an exact historical issue match to CRSP.

sources.title: Audit Analytics Data Dictionary: Disclosure Controls
sources.use: Provider-authored dictionary on university mirror, indexed text read via web search. Defines IS_EFFECTIVE and MATERIAL_WEAKNESS separately. Its remediation note says some registrants claim effective controls while a material weakness remains, and AA requires unequivocal adequate remediation before removing its flag. This supports preserving separate control effectiveness and material weakness states, not an automatic equivalence. It does not establish the exact numeric encoding in this local vintage.

sources.use: The exact local catalog labels IID as Header Primary Global Issue ID and HIID as Historic Primary Global Issue ID. This attempt uses HIID with dated CCM LIID evidence for historical primary-issue matching.

sources.use: Provider dictionary indexed text defines COMPANY_FKEY as SEC CIK and ticker as current as of the latest business day. Use verified CIK mapping for AA→Compustat rather than claiming a current ticker is historical. Also indexed in provider Auditor Changes/Engagements dictionaries on lipas.uwasa.fi.

sources.title: LPC/LoanConnector: Deal List Report
sources.use: Primary provider help distinguishes tranche and deal grain, original and converted amounts, selectable report currency, and current rating displays. Exact local catalog must identify which raw field/version is used; this help does not by itself prove historical rating or FacilityAmt exchange-rate semantics.

sources.title: S&P Research Insight North America Data Guide (2004): company and issue market value
sources.use: MKVAL uses primary price times quarterly company shares with a three-month reporting lag. MKVALM sums issue-level monthly price times shares over actively traded common issues; MKVALF selects MKVALM at fiscal year end. Inactive classes, fallback shares and ADR ratios matter. This 2004 guide does not establish the exact 1993 PST series used by Beaver/Ryan.

sources.title: WRDS: Using Compustat Historical Identifiers
sources.use: Compustat legacy CUSIP fields can contain the most recent identifier. SEC_IDHIST and SEC_HISTORY supply dated identifiers and primary-issue evidence. A historical accounting DATADATE does not make a header CUSIP historical; use effective identifier dates or CRSP NCUSIP/CCM.

sources.title: S&P Research Insight North America Data Guide (2004): geographic segment codes and assets
sources.use: Legacy GAREAG codes identify regions, domestic operations, and aggregate foreign segments; combined segments can carry several codes. Code98 is total foreign and code99 can duplicate it. IAG is identifiable segment assets in millions. These legacy definitions do not establish the current WRDS GEOTP coding; verify that separately.

sources.title: S&P Compustat Segment Information: segment, source, and geographic area records
sources.use: Primary provider document hosted by WRDS. SGEOTP:1=Total Foreign,2=Domestic,3=NonDomestic (physical5; Foreign wraps onto the next line). Distinct SGEOCD/SGEOAR fields identify actual countries/regions in a separate geographic-area file; customer geography is separate. Data year versus source year identifies restated vintages, and currency/source-currency fields differ. Verify local GEOTP mapping and observed labels before aggregation; do not sum total foreign plus its components.
sources.segment_type_use: Physical5 distinguishes BUSSEG legacy business/product lines, OPSEG mixed operating organization, GEOSEG geography, STSEG states. Physical7 separates data year/calendar year/source year and explains Jan–May fiscal-year labels refer to the previous calendar year. Do not combine overlapping source vintages or count geographic and business presentations as independent operating segments.

sources.title: Altman (1968), Financial Ratios, Discriminant Analysis and the Prediction of Corporate Bankruptcy
sources.use: Original formula and component definitions. X4 includes preferred and common equity market values; debt includes current and long term. The first four coefficients .012/.014/.033/.006 use percentage-valued ratios; see the author's later clarification below. Do not silently substitute the private-firm Z-prime model.

sources.title: Altman (July 2000), Predicting Financial Distress of Companies: Revisiting the Z-Score and ZETA Models
sources.use: Mirrored transcription of the author's research paper, sections X4 and A Clarification. For fractional ratios, coefficients are1.2/1.4/3.3/.6, with the original sales coefficient .999 (often rounded1). X4 denominator is total liabilities, numerator includes preferred/common equity market values. A common-equity-only or preferred-book-value fallback is an explicit approximation, not the exact original definition.

sources.title: S&P Research Insight2004: EPS share counts versus shares outstanding
sources.use: CSHO=A25 and CSHOQ=Q61 are end-period common shares. CSHPRI=A54 and CSHPRQ=Q15 are shares used for basic/primary EPS; CSHFD=A171 and CSHFDQ are diluted EPS shares. Do not map legacy A54 to CSHO. Source prose and item-number conflicts require explicit interpretation, not a silent substitution.

sources.title: S&P Compustat North America User’s Guide (2003)
sources.use: WCAPC legacyA236/Q73 excludes cash/currentdebt: cash-generating changes positive underSCF2/3/5, negative underSCF1. WCAPCH A180/Q101 totalsources-minususes includescash/currentdebt and appliesSCF1. Supports format-specific FOPT operatingcashflow adjustment ratherthan addingtotalWCAPCH. Quarterly statementfieldsYTD. ResearchInsight2004 wordingphysical899 is lessspecificaboutformat; retain originalpaper construction assumptions.

sources.title: S&P Compustat Xpressfeed: Understanding the Data (December 2007)
sources.use: Provider crosswalk names IDIT as Interest Income and NOPIO as Nonoperating Income (Expense) – Excluding Interest Income. Combined-items table for IDIT matches the legacy A62/IINT table: SALE, XINT, NOPI, NOPIO. Supports the modern North America mnemonic mapping; does not authorize zero-filling missing IDIT or interpreting NOPI−NOPIO as observed interest when combination codes are unavailable.
sources.split_adjustment_use: Provider lists AJEXDI/AJEXQ/AJEXM and division of per-share values versus multiplication of shares. Physical96 explains reversal of post-period stock splits in reported fundamental values. A within-issue source-date to anchor-date per-share rebase therefore multiplies by anchor factor/source factor; a cross-issue or cross-provider common terminal base is not established.

sources.title: S&P Research Insight2004: Order Backlog A98
sources.use: Annual item98 is OB (Order Backlog), millions of dollars at fiscal year end; includes sales and unfunded backlog. Paper variable BKLG is derived, not the raw Compustat field.

legacy_item_index_note: Machine-extracted annual-item locator index. Verify each cited page; omitted mappings require manual lookup. Cached 2004 provider PDF is in the same folder.

local_fx_coverage.note: Full-span bounded-field scan of the catalog-listed files. All monthly rows have GBP primary currency; USD and CAD monthly coverage begins January1982. Check actual required leg/date matches; global start alone is not sufficient coverage.

ibes_actual_basis_catalog_note.finding: Coordinator catalog check: all local IBES ACT/ACTU/RACT actual products lack a primary/diluted company-basis flag. DET/DETU PDF is estimate-level basis as received; provider guide says stored values are converted to company basis, so PDF does not establish actual basis. STATSUM ESTFLAG means primary/secondary estimate, not primary/diluted EPS. Do not substitute either flag for actual-basis evidence or choose GAAP EPS by closeness to the IBES value. A basic/primary approximation, if necessary, must be an explicit material limitation, as in W3121262606 A1.

bernard_autocorrelation.title: Bernard (1995), The Feltham–Ohlson Framework: Implications for Empiricists
bernard_autocorrelation.source_location: Physical page6 / printed738, Table1 note; scanned formula inspected visually
bernard_autocorrelation.interpretation: Annual coefficient-series standard error adjusted assuming AR(1), factor sqrt((1+phi)/(1-phi)-2*phi*(1-phi^n)/(n*(1-phi)^2)); phi is serial correlation and n is number of observations. This is not identical to Newey–West lag1. Formula supplies a finite-sample AR(1) factor but does not identify an installed Stata implementation.
